scenes.headline: How a looped Transformer buys depth with passes
scenes.sub: One core block, run again and again: injection, halting, truncated backprop
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Rutabaga! A looped Transformer runs one block over and over. Depth costs compute, not parameters.

scenes.text: Store a few layers and run them many times, feeding each pass's output back in, so depth is set by compute rather than by parameters.
scenes.say: The idea: store a few layers, run them many times, and feed each pass back in.

steps.say: The prelude embeds the tokens once, into a vector e.

steps.note: Huginn: 2 prelude, 4 core and 2 coda layers
steps.say: Each pass, the core reads its last state together with e. That's input injection.
Its output becomes the next state, and the same four layers run again.
After the last pass, the coda reads the state out as a next-token prediction.

scenes.title: Where the compute goes
scenes.text: FLOPs ≈ 2 x (prelude + r x core + coda)

parts.note: stored once, used r times per token
parts.say: The core's weights are stored once, but every token uses them r times.
The prelude and coda run once.

scenes.label: parameters' worth of compute per token, from 3.5 billion stored
scenes.say: At thirty-two passes, Huginn does the work of a fifty billion parameter model, from three and a half billion stored.

items.say: Sample how many passes to run, around thirty-two on average.
Backpropagate through only the last eight, so memory doesn't grow with depth.
The prelude still learns, because e enters every pass.

left.title: Fixed pass count
items: Every token runs the same passes
left.say: A fixed count is simple. But it spends the same on every token, and LOTUS gets worse run past its training depth.

right.title: Halting per token
items: Universal Transformer: a learned halting probability
Huginn: stop when two passes agree
right.say: Halting lets easy tokens stop early: a learned score in the Universal Transformer, or Huginn stopping once two passes agree.

scenes.text: A loop turns depth into a compute budget: more passes buy more computation, paid in FLOPs, latency and cache, never in weights.
scenes.say: A loop turns depth into a compute budget. You pay in FLOPs, latency and cache, never in weights.

recap: Inject the input at every pass
Truncated backprop; halting is still open
scenes.say: A shared core between a prelude and a coda. The input, every pass. Backprop through the last few.
